acceptance: The 0.6.0 wheel and sdist contain none of the four appendix SQL files, shown by a test over the built distributions.
A source checkout still has them and the TPC-DI rework tests that read them still pass.
No installed-distribution code path crashes on their absence.
description:
## Problem
BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4467 ships the TPC-DI appendix SQL (tpcdi_audit.sql, tpcdi_validation.sql, tpcdi_visibility_1.sql, tpcdi_visibility_2.sql) unmodified in benchbox/_binaries/tpc-di/ and _sources/tpc-di/. Their source is an unofficial shared copy, and tpcdi-settle-appendix-sql-source-20261121 forbids a release that includes them until the source is settled. TPC-DI is unavailable in 0.6.0, so no user path needs them.

## Owner decision (choice dialog, 2026-11-24)
"Exclude the four appendix SQL files from the 0.6.0 wheel and sdist; keep them in the repository for the rework. Settle the source before the release that reopens TPC-DI."

## Change
- Exclude exactly those four files from both distributions (package data and MANIFEST.in / sdist), keeping them in the repository and usable from a source checkout.
- Code that loads them (benchbox/core/tpcdi/appendix.py and its callers) must fail with a clear message, not a crash, when they are absent from an installed distribution. TPC-DI already refuses to run, so this only affects internal callers and tests.
- Keep the integrity manifest, NOTICE text and README licence section truthful for what each distribution contains.
- A test builds the wheel and the sdist (or inspects their file lists through the existing package checks) and asserts the four files are absent and the TPC-DI tools archive, EULA and NOTICE files are unchanged.
- Append to tpcdi-settle-appendix-sql-source-20261121 that the release gate is met by exclusion for 0.6.0; that item stays open for the reopening release.

## Guardrails
No change to the files themselves. Do not remove the TPC-DI tools archive or licence files. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; changelog fragment under Before you upgrade only if a user can observe it, otherwise internal.
